questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to travel to a place that made sense for my field of studies, since I specialise in East Asian theatre and performance styles, hence why I chose South Korea. I already had some proficiency in the Korean language, which made it easier to communicate with locals on my exchange and was another motivation for me to choose South Korea.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a great opportunity, and I learned so much more than I had expected. I know speak Korean much better and more confidently and have a much deeper and thorough understanding of the Korean language.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. Yonsei University was excellent at providing clear and comprehensive information regarding immegration and matriculation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university in Seoul offered to help with applying for a residence card, which made the process easier and less stressful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were limited options available since they could not guarantee housing, and it was necessary to apply the moment the application opened. They had two dorm buildings, one for only girls with shared rooms (2 per room) and common bathrooms, and then another one for both boys and girls with both shared and individual rooms and private bathrooms. I lived in the first and enjoyed it a lot.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were communal kitchens, but I did not use them since there was only one per building. Other than that, there was a canteen on weekdays, and a few restaurants in the area, and more 15 minutes' walk away.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you want to cook, I would find an off-campus house, or be prepared to share a kitchen with everyone in the building. Apply the moment the application opens, and be prepared to live with students from different countries.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had a complicated system, but after watching a tutorial, it became easy. I only know the first part well, since I was lucky to get all my courses on the first try. As students, you are given a specific amount of points, and then once it opens, you have to bid on the courses and depending on how many points and how many people bid, the courses are distributed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an online tutorial

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Super successful, I got all my classes on the first try

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Watch the video tutorials beforehand, and be ready when it opens and be quick. So, prepare ahead and have backup courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was about the same as at KU, but it was more about learning things by heart than using the knowledge actively.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was less interactive and more just a professor talking for three hours, and asking a few questions. But the professors were always willing to answer questions, and it was interesting.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender from Antiquity to the present
History of Korean Religion
Korean Popular Culture and Cultural Translations
Korean Language Intensive

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think all of them, since the first two give a good insight into the modern Korean society, by tracing trends from ancient times. The third one was great in understanding why Korean modern media is popular internationally, and Korean was just good for training the language while being in Korea.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Printing, I needed assignments printed out and notes for exams

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was cheaper than expected, and the Korean mandatory health care was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A few international clubs and sports were available in English, but not many.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The mentor club, since it paired 10 students up with a Korean student and the groups then had small meetings where they went out for activities together. It was a great way of both meeting locals and other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Since South Korea is relatively small, it is easy and not super expensive to travel by bus around the country, so I recommend seeing more of the country outside of Seoul or just visiting museums or palaces in the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy since I have travelled to Asia before, but not cooking a lot was the most difficult, and the food was sweeter than at home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid of talking to others, try to join clubs or engage with classmates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The classes and getting to explore the country

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Apply for housing the moment the application opens; don't wait until the morning, because the rooms go fast.
2. Find backup courses, since it is not guaranteed that you will get your first choice.
3. Be ready to write exams by hand

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I got to better my Korean and learn so much more about the culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Eating out every day and all the bread being sweet

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
